cards.claim: Optimal scaling strategy is critically task-dependent; generation requires data size to grow 3-5× faster than classification optimal setups
cards.conditions: Image classification vs. generation tasks at fixed resolution (32×32)
cards.effect: Generation requires 3-5× faster data scaling rate than classification for equivalent performance
cards.evidence: Empirical finding from scaling experiments across compute budgets up to 7e19 FLOPs
cards.quote: optimal scaling strategy is critically task-dependent. At a fixed resolution of 32x32 alone, the optimal scaling properties for image classification and image generation diverge, where generation optimal setup requires the data size grow three to five times faster than for the classification optimal setup.

cards.claim: As image resolution increases, model size must grow much faster than data size in the optimal scaling strategy
cards.effect: Model capacity scaling must outpace data size scaling; non-linear relationship between model width and data requirements
cards.evidence: Empirical finding from multi-resolution scaling experiments
cards.quote: as image resolution increases, the optimal scaling strategy indicates that the model size must grow much faster than data size.

cards.claim: The primary bottleneck limiting performance is compute rather than training data quantity
cards.conditions: Scaling experiments across full compute budget range (up to 7e19 FLOPs)
cards.effect: Performance gains are compute-limited; increasing data without proportional compute gains yields diminishing returns
cards.evidence: Projection and finding from scaling study across compute budgets
cards.quote: the primary bottleneck is compute rather than the amount of training data.
